summary.headline: J. Kumar Infraprojects Q1 FY27 revenue rose 2% to INR1,511 crores while EBITDA margin slipped to 14.1%, with FY27 revenue guidance held at 15% growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 2% YoY to INR1,511 crores and EBITDA dipped 1% to INR215 crores, with margin down 50 bps to 14.1%. PAT fell 6% to INR97 crores, which management attributed to timing factors and project mix. Management blamed a temporary BMC water-usage ban and approval delays on GMLR and VDCR for slower execution. It kept FY27 revenue growth guidance at 15% (about INR6,500 crores) and an order inflow target of INR8,000-10,000 crores, and pushed the INR7,500 crores revenue goal from FY27 to FY28.

financial_highlights.value: Negative INR45 crores (net cash) as on June 30, 2026

financial_highlights.change: Up from about INR580 crores at March 2026
Management expects FY27 to be similar to FY26 after TBM capitalisation

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Elevated corridors and flyovers 48%, roads and road tunnels 20%, metro (elevated and underground) 9%, others 23%.

segments.name: Chennai project
segments.commentary: NHAI packages worth INR3,570 crores, about 20% complete, completion extended to December 2028 due to Cooum river restrictions; state package of INR580 crores about 65% complete, due March 2027. Prolongation cost received from NHAI.

segments.name: GMLR (Mumbai, tunnelling)
segments.commentary: About 26% complete per management; first TBM ready for launch pending political approval, second TBM to launch in about 2 months. Internal target June 2029, contractual max December 2029 after extension.

segments.name: Anand Nagar-Saket (Mulund)
segments.commentary: About 15% complete; scheduled completion October/November 2028 with 3 km of 8.5 km cleared after NHAI-MMRDA toll issue resolved.

segments.name: Vadhvan port project
segments.commentary: Mobilisation under way; excavation to start only in October 2026 after monsoon. About 6-7 km of the 32 km stretch has land acquisition pending.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 15% YoY (about INR6,500 crores) reiterated; management said Q2 growth will also be positive and H2 more visible as Vadhvan and new projects ramp up.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 14-15%; management targets a further 50-100 bps improvement over time.
FY27 order inflow target of INR8,000-10,000 crores; current tally is about INR7,000 crores including L1 for the INR1,500 crores DMRC underground job, expected to convert in Q2.
INR7,500 crores revenue target moved from FY27 to FY28 at similar 14-15% EBITDA margin; management indicated INR1,000-1,500 crores EBITDA for FY28 is consistent with the pipeline.
Working capital days to stay in the 100-110 range; gross debt expected to stay below INR800 crores by year-end as term loans amortise.
Depreciation expected to rise from about INR50 crores to about INR60 crores per quarter once the INR300 crores TBM is capitalised.
Capex of about INR150 crores per year for the next two years including maintenance capex of about INR100 crores; no major new capex unless a large new project needs new equipment.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex was INR34 crores; FY27 and FY28 capex guided at about INR150 crores per year including INR100 crores maintenance.
Capital work in progress of about INR300 crores (TBM) to be capitalised within a week or so of TBM launch, adding to depreciation.
Non-fund based limit INR5,000 crores, 65% utilised; fund based limit INR1,300 crores, 39% utilised.
Management said current machinery is sufficient for the order book including L1 and no large capex is needed for repeat projects.
Mobilisation advance of INR470 crores, all interest-bearing, at roughly 8.5-10% (MCLR plus about 3%); management says none exceeds 10%.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 order inflow about INR5,500 crores, plus INR1,500 crores L1 for DMRC underground metro (ex-GST; INR1,770 crores including GST per management); INR2,000 crores of bids submitted.

Management flagged INR50,000-1,00,000 crores of upcoming opportunities over 9-12 months, including MSRDC (Shaktipeeth), Uttan-Virar corridor (about INR15,000-16,000 crores), NHAI and DMRC work; timing could slip 3-6 months.
Management said margins will not be sacrificed for volume and that it will not chase orders at thin margins.
Management said the company works in seven states; Maharashtra remains the preferred market.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue been flat for FY26 despite a strong order book, and what is different now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said big-ticket orders from FY24 (GMLR, VDCR, Chennai elevated corridor) were delayed by land acquisition, tree-cutting permissions and GAD finalisation. VDCR is still slow but management expects it to be on track in 1-2 months and to push from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% FY27 revenue growth achievable given Q1 was 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 will be more visible, Q2 growth will still be positive, and 15%+ is achievable by year-end, with FY27 and FY28 both expected at about 15% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will the working capital cycle and gross debt come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is 103 days, targeted at 100-110 days. Gross debt rose to about INR840 crores because of the TBM instalment paid in late June. Management expects it to stay below INR800 crores by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate and other income outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax rate expected to be similar to FY26 for the full year, falling from 29.7% once the INR300 crores TBM is capitalised. Other income of INR19 crores in Q1 is recurring, mainly interest on FDs held as margin for non-fund-based limits.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering a buyback or fund raise?
qa_highlights.answer: A buyback is 'on our cards' but deferred for now given order-related capital needs. The fund raise is not being pursued for the moment.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cancelled or on-hold MMRDA order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no MMRDA order is on hold. The only pending award is the DMRC underground job of INR1,500 crores (ex-GST), expected in Q2 FY27.

risks_watch: Revenue ramp risk: Q1 FY27 growth was only 2% and FY27 guidance of 15% (about INR6,500 crores) needs roughly 20%+ growth in the remaining three quarters; watch whether Q2 growth is positive as guided.

Order conversion: the INR1,500 crores DMRC underground job (L1, ex-GST) is expected in Q2 FY27 and is tied to World Bank funding clearances; the INR8,000-10,000 crores inflow target depends on large pipeline awards that management said could slip 3-6 months.

Project execution: VDCR is described as slow and expected to pick up in 1-2 months; GMLR first TBM launch awaits political approval; Vadhvan excavation only from October 2026 with 6-7 km of the 32 km stretch still under land acquisition.
Balance sheet: gross debt rose to about INR840 crores from INR580 crores in March; management guides below INR800 crores by year-end. Working capital at 103 days vs a 100-110 day target.

Margin and tax: EBITDA margin fell 50 bps to 14.1%; FY27 guidance 14-15%. Effective tax rate of 29.7% expected to fall once the INR300 crores TBM is capitalised, and depreciation to rise from about INR50 crores to about INR60 crores per quarter.
key_quotes: So overall by the year end 15% plus is very much achievable.
We will keep our topline flat and there will be some minus that will work, but opportunities are there that we won't see such days.
Unless we make margins, we don't want growth.
There is no order of MMRDA which is on hold for us.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and assertive on order inflows, the 15% FY27 growth target and margin discipline, repeatedly stating it will not chase thin-margin orders. It was more cautious and evasive on timing: it tied the revenue slowdown to land acquisition, tree-cutting and GAD delays, deferred pipeline timing as outside its control, and declined to commit beyond the INR8,000-10,000 crores order target, preferring to speak after Q2.

adds.what: INR300 crores TBM (tunnel boring machine) for GMLR, capitalised within a week or so of launch; first TBM pending political approval, second TBM to launch in abo

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth of 15% (~INR6,500 crore) is held, backed by a INR22,246 crore order book and INR1,500 crore DMRC L1 (not yet converted), but Q1 revenue grew only 2% and the INR7,500 crore target has slipped to FY28; the only capacity addition is a INR300 crore TBM, and the brief gives no utilisation figure.
